ranked.headline: Benchmark design, not architecture, drives validity of biological response models
ranked.summary: Single-cell perturbation and chemotherapy response benchmarks show that splits, metrics, and baselines now determine whether reported gains hold.

ranked.headline: Heterogeneous biological features fused in learned models for interaction prediction
ranked.summary: February 2026 items couple multimodal inputs with graph and transformer models across drug, protein and gene prediction tasks.

ranked.headline: Computational single-cell methods expose aging-linked states and technical artifacts
ranked.summary: Public scRNA and snRNA datasets now yield conserved aging-relevant cell states, while new tools address artifacts and spatial marker discovery.

ranked.headline: Inferring cancer genome state and mutation consequences from large sequencing data
ranked.summary: Single-cell and patient-scale sequencing now resolves oncogene amplification, two-hit loss, and mutation-level TF binding effects in tumors.

ranked.headline: Learned models infer pathogen and microbial properties directly from sequence data
ranked.summary: Surveillance-scale datasets, from wastewater sequencing to outbreak spectra and phage databases, are testing how far sequence-level inference can reach.

ranked.headline: Reference-flexible methods resolve haplotypes, crossovers, and population structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend variant and haplotype inference to unrelated individuals, pangenomes, and short tandem repeats.

ranked.headline: Calibrated, ancestry-aware methods map variants to disease genes and traits
ranked.summary: Large-scale variant effect data, ancestry-stratified predictor benchmarks, and whole-genome models now test variant-to-phenotype inference directly.

ranked.headline: Learned representations are applied to classify diverse biological sequence data
ranked.summary: Five recent items apply protein language models, CNNs, transformers and taxonomy-guided features to enzyme, virus, barcode and microbiome classification.

ranked.headline: ML and generative models now target ligand, peptide, and cyclopeptide design
ranked.summary: Co-folding and generative models are being tested on input representation and on peptide and small-molecule design outputs checked against experiment.

ranked.headline: Computational prioritization of candidate targets in aging, liver disease, and Long COVID
ranked.summary: Multi-omic, causal-genetic, metabolic-model, and network analyses now nominate candidate targets from existing data, with a shared computational emphasis.

ranked.headline: Resistance and host-linking inferred directly from raw sequencing reads without assembly
ranked.summary: Read-level methods now infer resistance determinants and host associations from raw sequencing without requiring assembly.

ranked.headline: Physical models link cadherin junction dynamics and nuclear mechanics to cell states
ranked.summary: Recent mechanistic models quantify adhesion, nuclear envelope mechanics, and tissue stratification forces underlying cell state transitions.

ranked.headline: Directional, dynamic and critical markers of functional brain interaction across…
ranked.summary: Directional, time-varying and scaling-based connectivity measures are now validated across LFP, MEG, EEG, fMRI and whole-cortex models.

ranked.headline: Software tools tracking molecules, filopodia, and colonies in microscopy data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications report software for single-molecule tracking, 4D filopodia tracing, colony segmentation, and spatial transcriptomics…

ranked.headline: Synteny-aware comparative genomics ties gene evolution to conserved genomic context
ranked.summary: Near chromosome-scale assemblies and synteny-aware analyses now position lineage-specific and venom genes within conserved genomic context.

ranked.headline: Learned sequence models extend to peptide, codon, and oligonucleotide design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair flow matching, reinforcement learning, and LLM benchmarking with sequence and binder design across biomolecule classes.

ranked.headline: Inferring regulatory states from indirect single-cell, spatial and cfDNA proxies
ranked.summary: New items replace direct assays with proxies, including cfDNA chromatin marks, Perturb-seq instrumental variables and multiscale spatial metrics.

ranked.headline: Genomic language models gain from region-aware compression and k-mer downsampling
ranked.summary: Recent preprints address the cost of long genomic contexts, token choice, and compact representations for bacterial phenotype prediction.

ranked.headline: Long-read and short-read methods refine variant, isoform and splicing inference
ranked.summary: Long-read sequencing and transfer of established RNA-seq models are extending variant, isoform and splicing analysis to new settings.

ranked.headline: Microbial genomes and community models link gut functions to host and probiotic outcomes
ranked.summary: Population-scale genome collections and community-scale metabolic models are now being paired to test host-microbiome associations and probiotic efficacy.

ranked.headline: Probabilistic modeling and scalable algorithms for proteomics and metabolomics inference
ranked.summary: Newly reported tools tie identification and quantitation to explicit measurement models while scaling to hundreds of millions of spectra.

ranked.headline: Gene model curation and comparative annotation underpin reliable orthology analyses
ranked.summary: Three recent items report annotation error accounting, community curation, and taxonomically broad gene annotation for comparative analyses.

ranked.headline: Generative and graph models advance molecular design and atom-level interpretability
ranked.summary: Generative and graph-based models now target validity, interpretability and experimentally relevant molecular properties.

ranked.headline: Archaic introgression and environment shape immune eQTLs in Indonesian individuals
ranked.summary: Expanding population datasets and new simulators for immune and viral sequence evolution are sharpening how genetic and immune diversity is modelled.

ranked.headline: Trap spaces and information principles formalize cell-state transitions and regulation
ranked.summary: Quantitative models now tie measurable biomarkers and transcriptomic time series to defined cellular phenotypes and fate decisions.

ranked.headline: Simulations tie membrane environment to lipid protonation and outer membrane organization
ranked.summary: Constant-pH and coarse-grained simulations now resolve membrane-dependent protonation and lipid redistribution in envelope-relevant models.

ranked.headline: Learned models infer volumes, tilts and coordinates from cryo-EM and cryo-ET density
ranked.summary: Five preprints apply deep generative and supervised models directly to experimental cryo-EM and cryo-ET density.

ranked.headline: Experimental restraints and ensemble sampling refine protein structure predictions
ranked.summary: Four 2026 items pair experimental or quantum-mechanical data with AlphaFold, Rosetta, and MD to refine structural models.

ranked.headline: Tools test ChIP-seq peak equivalence, impute methylation gaps, map TE-epigenome links
ranked.summary: Recent releases package specific epigenomic and genotyping analyses into tools with CLI, GUI, or web interfaces for expert users.

ranked.headline: Single-cell models extend to multimodal profiling, batch correction and spatial data
ranked.summary: Learned single-cell representations are being extended to paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq, batch correction, and spatial transcriptomics.

ranked.headline: Simulations link peptide sequence to phase behavior and membrane translocation
ranked.summary: Sequence patterning metrics and enhanced-sampling simulations now quantify how composition governs condensation and membrane barrier crossing.

ranked.headline: Interactive tools make alignment, motif and knockout phenotype data explorable
ranked.summary: Recent releases pair command-line or web interfaces with alignment, motif, regulatory-model and knockout phenotype datasets for direct exploration.

ranked.headline: Learned models span RNA folding, protein epistasis, antibody paratopes, and PIWI cleavage
ranked.summary: Zero-shot predictors fail on strongly epistatic mutations, while pretrained protein language models now capture viral evolution and paratope features.

ranked.headline: Open computational tools for variant effect, enrichment, and motif-domain annotation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published tool extend pipeline-based variant and annotation analysis to rice breeding, protein families, and metabolomics.

ranked.headline: Simulations reveal how caveolin, PNPLA and endophilin remodel membranes
ranked.summary: Multiscale MD now resolves how curvature-generating and lipid-targeting proteins engage ER, lipid droplet and scission-relevant membranes.

ranked.headline: Physics-informed and phasor methods unmix spectral signatures in biological imaging
ranked.summary: Multiplexed fluorescence and photoacoustic imaging generate overlapping spectral signals that now require unsupervised or physics-constrained separation.

ranked.headline: LLM agents and knowledge graphs enforce provenance in biomedical claim generation
ranked.summary: Multi-agent LLM frameworks now generate provenance-traced biomedical claims, extending to Perturb-seq prediction and knowledge-graph enrichment.

ranked.headline: Machine learning prioritizes TDP-43 inhibitors and designs GPCR-targeted modulators
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs safety-aware QSAR and hybrid GNN screening with deep learning protein design for receptor modulators.

ranked.headline: Data-structure engineering speeds exact and optimal sequence and graph alignment
ranked.summary: Pangenome alignment sets reach hundreds of millions of records, pressing runtime and storage demands on exact graph and local alignment tools.

ranked.headline: Mapping regulatory consequences of noncoding GWAS variants in disease loci
ranked.summary: Recent preprints pair biobank GWAS and brain RNA-seq with CRISPRi and Hi-C to test which regulatory step each noncoding variant perturbs.
